summary.short: Illinois statute under which the Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity grants tax exemptions and credits to qualifying data centers that meet capital investment, job creation and green-standard conditions. Credits apply from taxable years beginning in 2019; no new certificates after July 1, 2029.
summary.long: Directs the Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity to issue certificates of exemption from specified Illinois retailers' occupation, use and service taxes and a credit certification against income taxes for qualifying Illinois data centers, and to award income tax credits for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2019 (a, b). A qualifying data center must be located in Illinois, make a capital investment of at least $250,000,000 over a 60-month period, create at least 20 full-time or equivalent jobs with total compensation of at least 120% of the county average wage, and within 2 years of being placed in service certify carbon neutrality or a listed green building standard (c). Certificates last no more than 20 calendar years, and the Department and the applicant must enter a memorandum of understanding that includes a repayment obligation if goals are not met (d). The Department must report annually to the Governor and General Assembly from July 1, 2021 (e). Contractors must comply with responsible bidder requirements, and rehabilitation or construction must be under a project labor agreement (f, g). Annual reports on tax benefits are due by May 31, and failure to report may result in suspension or revocation (h). No new certificates may be issued after July 1, 2029 (i), and the Department must adopt rules (j).
